spindle.observe.AnswerSource.title: AnswerSource
spindle.observe.AnswerSource.description: What answered one external cause of a served command. `world`: the `decisions` of the world the last reset loaded, `spindle.console.World`. `file`: the decisions file. `default`: the default branch `--answer-default` takes. `call`: the HTTP call the environment binds the cause to (`[http.<name>]`). `unanswered`: nothing did, or the cause's HTTP call failed, and the command answered `501`. Source: `crates/spindle-cli/src/decisions.rs:47-71`, `crates/spindle-ingress/src/observe.rs:186-213`.

spindle.observe.ExternalAnswer.title: ExternalAnswer
spindle.observe.ExternalAnswer.description: One external cause a command asked about while a served request was answered, and what answered it.

command.description: The qualified command that asked: the routed command, or one an event binding invoked while the request was answered; the `command` label of `spindle_external_causes_total`.

outcome.description: The outcome whose cause was asked about, as the command declares it.

holds.description: Whether the cause holds; absent when nothing answered it.

spindle.observe.OperationKind.title: OperationKind
spindle.observe.OperationKind.description: What a routed request was for.

spindle.observe.RefusedBound.title: RefusedBound
spindle.observe.RefusedBound.description: One command an event binding invoked that was refused on its last attempt, so nothing it would have written was written: refused by an outcome that declares an error, or rejected by the kernel, which selected no outcome (an input, guard or invariant it could not satisfy). The command that published the event stays committed, and the event log (`GET /api/events`) lists only the events the run committed. ESS defines no observable result for a refused bound command; this entry is Spindle's (`docs/design/spindle.md` § 11, refused bound command). It names the error and never a value of its fields.

component.description: The component that accepts the command.

command.description: The qualified name of the refused command.

caused_by.description: The qualified command whose run published the event the binding carried: the routed command, or one an event binding invoked on the way. Absent where the event was published in another process of a run split over processes.

outcome.description: The refusing outcome the model selected; absent where the kernel rejected it.

error.description: The qualified name of the error that outcome declares; absent where the kernel rejected it.

kind.description: Where the kernel rejected it, the kind of its error, as `spindle_command_failures_total` labels it (`invalid_input`, `undecidable`, `undecided`, `no_value`, `invalid_value`, `broken_invariant`, `undeclared`, `unsupported`, `store`, `not_granted`, `unknown_command`); absent where an outcome refused it.

attempts.description: How many times it was run, the last included: more than 1 only where the binding retries.

spindle.observe.RequestClass.title: RequestClass
spindle.observe.RequestClass.description: How a served run answered one request; the class follows who answered, not the status. `served`: the model answered it, with an outcome the command declares or the view's rows, whatever status the binding gives that outcome, `501` and `503` included. `refused`: the ingress or ESS's standard refusal answered it `4xx` before the model did, other than `not-granted`. `not-granted`: `403` "not granted", no grant admits the actor. `not-served`: spindle's own `501`, for an operation this ingress cannot route, the kernel does not run or the host does not read, or for an external cause nothing answered. `failed`: a `5xx` spindle itself answered, other than that `501`. `unrouted`: no route has the path, or not under that method.

spindle.observe.RequestRecord.title: RequestRecord
spindle.observe.RequestRecord.description: One request a served run answered, as `GET /__spindle/requests` lists it. Requests under `/__spindle/` are not recorded.

sequence.description: Monotonic per run, starting at 0; a gap in a list is a request the ring dropped.

at.description: When the request's head was read.

path.description: What the record keeps of the request's path, without the query string: the route template it resolved to (`/loans/{id}`), never the path with the resource identifiers in it; for an unrouted request its first segment, with `/…` after it where the path has more (`/loans/…`). At most 2,048 bytes, cut on a character boundary with `…` where longer.

query.description: The query string of a console request (`/api/model`, `/api/events`, `/api/reset`), absent where it carried none and for every other request. Each pair is kept in order, empty pairs dropped: `after` and `limit` by name, the value of `after` where the request was answered `200` (a cursor `GET /api/events` answered) and the value of `limit` where it is digits; every other name and value is written `…`. At most 2,048 bytes, as the path, cut with `…` where longer.

route.description: The route template the path resolved to; absent for an unrouted request.

operation.description: The qualified command or view the route is bound to, or the console route as `GET /api/model`; absent for an unrouted request.

outcome.description: The outcome the model selected, for a command it answered.

reason.description: Why the request was not served, for every class but `served`: the `refused` text of the answer, its words and the names it gives (a field, a type, a route) kept. A value the caller sent is never recorded: every value in the text (a quoted string, a list, an object, a number, `true`, `false` or `null`), and every map key, struct member or input field name the caller sent, is written `…`. At most 512 bytes, cut with `…` where longer. So the record of a refused request holds its method, its path (at most 2,048 bytes) and the names of its route, and under 1 KiB besides, whatever its body held.

duration_us.description: From the request's head read to its answer handed back, in microseconds.

events.description: The qualified names of the events the command published, in order.

externals.description: Every external cause asked while the request was answered, in the order asked: by the routed command and by every command an event binding invoked on the way.

unmet.description: Every event binding whose input was unmet while the request was answered, in the order the runtime reported them: bindings of the events the routed command published and of the events every command an event binding invoked on the way published. Empty when every binding's input was met. The list is complete when everything the request led to has run, and when it stopped because bindings kept triggering each other. When the routed command was kept and carrying its events on then failed, because the link to another component failed, a component's state could not be read or written, or another component stopped answering, the bindings found unmet before that failure are not listed.

refused_bound.description: Every command an event binding invoked while the request was answered that was refused on its last attempt: first those a refusing outcome refused, then those the kernel rejected, each in the order the runtime reported them. Empty when every one ran. Each is counted in `spindle_bound_refusals_total`. The list is complete when everything the request led to has run. When it stopped because bindings kept triggering each other, only the kernel's rejections before that are listed; when it failed as `unmet` says, none is. A command a timer fired, and one refused in another process of a run split over processes, is in no record.

spindle.observe.UnmetInput.title: UnmetInput
spindle.observe.UnmetInput.description: One event binding whose command input the event did not fill: a required field absent, a value carried across a declared conversion that is no value of the input's type, or a payload condition (`when.where`) that decides Unknown on the event, such as a comparison that reads an absent or `null` Optional field (`spindle_channel::Route::holds`). The command is not invoked: zero attempts, no retry, and the event's other bindings still run; the command that published the event stays committed. ESS 0.90.0 calls this an unmet binding-input obligation, with no attempt and no policy, only for a binding whose failure policy is chosen per refusal, answers the same failure of every other binding unsupported, and defines no observable result for either (`crates/verify/ess-conformance/src/interpret/bindings.rs`). The rule for every binding and this answer are Spindle's (`docs/design/spindle.md` § 11, unmet binding input; `spindle_channel::Unmet`).

component.description: The component that accepts the command.

command.description: The qualified name of the command not invoked.

reason.description: Why the input could not be filled, as the runtime words it, bounded as a record's `reason` is: its words and the names it gives (the binding, the input, a type) kept, a value the event carried never recorded: every value in the text (a quoted string, a list, an object, a number, `true`, `false` or `null`) is written `…`. At most 512 bytes, cut with `…` where longer.
